name: product-take
title: Product Take
description: One continuous take of a live interface: the product's own HTML, not a screenshot. The scene's beats drive it in order: the cursor travels and clicks, text is typed, the interface changes state, parts of it arrive, a chart is drawn, a figure counts up, and the camera follows the action, turning and pulling focus as it goes. The film's own lines can be set in the frame beside it, and the take can end by resolving the interface into the brand's own mark.

variables.label: Screen
variables.description: Supplied by the compiler from the scene's screen.

variables.label: Screen geometry
variables.description: Supplied by the compiler: the screen's size and regions as JSON.

variables.label: Beats
variables.description: Supplied by the compiler from the scene's beats.

variables.label: Opening state
variables.description: The state the interface is in when the take starts. Empty uses the page's own.

variables.label: Start framing
variables.description: The region the camera frames at the start. window is the whole interface.

variables.label: Frame fill
variables.description: How much of the frame the framed region may take, by width or height. Lower leaves more space around it.

variables.label: Closest zoom
variables.description: The camera never magnifies the interface beyond this, so close-ups keep their surroundings and stay readable.

variables.label: Side
variables.description: Where in the frame the interface sits. Put it to one side when the film's own lines share the frame; a camera beat can change it.

options.label: Left, with room on the right
Right, with room on the left

variables.label: Window
variables.description: Draw the interface inside an application window, or bare.

variables.label: Corner radius
variables.description: Corner radius of what is shown, in the screenshot's pixels. Match the isolated component's own corners.

variables.label: Perspective
variables.description: The angle the interface is seen from when the take starts. A camera beat can turn it to another angle.

options.label: Lying on a desk, seen from above at an angle

variables.label: Focus
variables.description: Which part of the frame is sharp when the take starts. A camera beat can pull focus.

options.label: A sharp band across the middle
Sharp below, soft at the top (the far edge)

variables.label: Slow push
variables.description: A slow, constant push-in under every camera move, so the picture never comes to a dead stop while text is typed or read.

variables.label: Light spill
variables.description: The screen throws a soft light in the film's accent on the stage around it. For a dark stage, so the interface belongs to it.

variables.label: Accent colour
variables.description: The film's one accent. Used for emphasis only.
